objectives: Explain how Q,K,V come from the same sequence
Trace how every token attends to every other

slides.title: Part 1 — Attention turned on itself
slides.body: Self-attention is the special case that powers every transformer: the query, key, and value sequences are *the same sequence*. Every token attends to every other token in one parallel operation — the property RNNs and CNNs could never achieve cheaply.

slides.title: Full reach in one layer
slides.body:
In **self-attention**, $Q$, $K$, $V$ are all projections of the *same* input. So every token can pull information from every other token in a single operation.

Why this is so powerful: an RNN passes information one step at a time (token 100 hears about token 1 only after 99 sequential steps). A CNN sees a fixed window. Self-attention has **full, parallel reach**.

The heatmap shows a self-attention matrix with a locality bias — most weight near the diagonal. Self-attention *can* be local like this or reach far back; the training signal decides.

slides.title: Every row is a distribution over the sequence
slides.body:
Each row of a self-attention matrix is a **probability distribution over the entire input**, including the token itself (the diagonal). The output at position $i$ is a weighted blend of *all* tokens' value vectors, with the model choosing the weights.

The diagonal carries identity meaning here — *"my own information is relevant to me."* In cross-attention (decoder attending to encoder) there is no diagonal preference, because Q and K come from different sequences. Self-attention is the only flavor where position $i$ attending to position $i$ means "myself."

slides.title: Part 2 — Causal masking: don't peek at the future
The mask
slides.body:
For **autoregressive** generation, predicting token 5 must not see tokens 6, 7, 8 — they don't exist yet at inference. The fix is a **causal mask**: before softmax, every cell above the diagonal is set to $-\infty$. After softmax those become exactly 0.

Each token attends to itself and all *earlier* positions, never later. During training this lets the model predict every position in parallel while each prediction only looks backward. **Encoder** transformers (BERT) skip the mask; **decoder** transformers (GPT) require it. The viz again — imagine the upper triangle blacked out.

question.question: In causal self-attention, can the token at position 3 attend to the token at position 7?
options: No — position 7 is in the future and is masked out
Yes — every token attends to every other token
Only if positions 4, 5, 6 are also attended to
question.explanation: Causal masking zeros attention from position i to any j > i. Position 3 may attend to 0,1,2,3 — never 4+. This is exactly what makes the model autoregressive: a prediction can only depend on the past.

question.question: Sort each transformer family by whether its self-attention uses a causal mask.

items.label: Encoder stack of a translation model

question.explanation: Autoregressive decoders (GPT, LLaMA) must not see the future, so they mask. Encoders (BERT, the encoder side of a seq2seq model) classify/encode a complete input, so every token may see every other — no mask.

slides.title: Part 3 — The quadratic wall
slides.body: Self-attention's power has a price that shapes the entire modern architecture landscape.

slides.title: O(n²) and the innovations that fight it
slides.body:
Self-attention is $O(n^2)$ in sequence length: 1,000 tokens → a million scores; 100,000 tokens → ten billion. This is *the* transformer bottleneck. Recent architecture work mostly attacks it:

- **FlashAttention** — same math, reordered so the full $n\times n$ matrix is never materialized (an IO/memory win, not an approximation).
- **Grouped/Multi-Query attention** — share K and V across heads to shrink the KV-cache.
- **Sliding-window attention** — restrict each token to a local window (breaks the quadratic, loses global reach).
- **Linear-attention / SSMs (Mamba, Performer)** — replace softmax with kernels for $O(n)$, at some quality cost.

Full $O(n^2)$ attention is still the quality gold standard when compute allows; everything else is a measured trade-off.

question.question: FlashAttention makes long-context attention much cheaper in memory. How?
options: It computes exact attention but never materializes the full n×n score matrix — it tiles the computation to stay in fast SRAM
It approximates softmax with a linear kernel
It drops attention to a local window
question.explanation: FlashAttention is exact — same result as standard attention. The win is systems-level: it fuses the softmax and matmul and tiles them so the giant n×n matrix never leaves fast on-chip memory, cutting memory traffic dramatically. It does not change the math, unlike sliding-window or linear-attention approximations.

question.question: From attention to SELF-attention
question.goal: You already derived attention; specialize it to one sequence attending to itself.

steps.prompt: In self-attention, where do Q, K, V come from?
steps.motivation: All three are linear projections of the SAME input — every token queries the same set it belongs to.

options: All three are linear projections of the same input sequence
Q from input, K/V from separate memory

steps.reveal: Q=XWq, K=XWk, V=XWv from the same X — each token attends over the whole sequence (incl. itself).

steps.prompt: Why is self-attention permutation-equivariant, and what fixes it?
steps.motivation: It is a set operation with no built-in order; order must be injected explicitly.

rubricCriteria.description: it treats the input as a set — no inherent order
so order must be added explicitly to the embeddings

hints: Shuffle the tokens — does the math change?
steps.reveal: No positional term ⇒ permuting inputs permutes outputs identically; positional encodings break that symmetry.

question.finalResult: Self-attention = Attention(XWq, XWk, XWv) — one sequence attending to itself

every token attends to every token, including itself

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body:
- **Self-attention**: Q, K, V from one sequence — every token mixes with every other in one parallel op.
- Each output row is a **distribution over the whole sequence**, diagonal included.
- **Causal masking** (upper triangle → −∞) makes decoders autoregressive; encoders go unmasked.
- Cost is **$O(n^2)$** — the bottleneck behind FlashAttention, GQA, sliding-window, and SSMs.

**Next:** [Multi-head attention](/wiki/multi-head-attention) — run many of these in parallel so one layer can learn many patterns at once.
